headline: Berkshire's profits dip 5.8% but Abel doubles buybacks to $9.6B; stocks bounce after an AI rout; Constellation, KKR, Rocket Lab and more report Monday
top_call: Berkshire Hathaway's operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.7 billion as GEICO had a rough quarter, but that was already priced into estimates, and Greg Abel answered by buying back $9.6 billion of stock, more than double last quarter. Railroad, energy and manufacturing all grew. Plain-English explainer below, plus who reports Monday.
subject: Berkshire: Penny beat, buybacks doubled · earnings, explained
backdrop: Friday's bounce: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq gained 1.1% after Thursday's AI-led rout pushed it into a correction, while the Dow slipped 0.5%. October payrolls jumped 165,000 vs about 59,000 expected and unemployment dipped to 4.1% — strong enough to push December rate-hike odds to about 77% on CME FedWatch. Still the S&P's worst week since June.
on_deck_sub: Who reports Monday, Nov 9, and what Wall Street expects
